note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative; jurisdiction unspecified. The notification route, its stops and its dates are supplied and editable placeholders drawn in the configured order ('Sequence as configured (illustrative)'); nothing states a valid method, a required form, a deadline, 'deemed' service or any effect. 'Questioned' only means that someone questions the communication in this configured example: a neutral ◆ chip and a dashed outline on the supplied leg, never a verdict. Coordinator standing rule (AUTHORING item 20): long-labels-stress is capped in one field. True driver, measured on the layout at 1:1 (the densest frame; heads >= 52 px rendered and text >= 16 px required): with four near-maximum date labels (35–38 characters) the legs' calendar under the flat track needs more room than lies between the file's path and the floor (best flat layout: text 18.9 px, heads ~54 px, calendar overflowing — 'cal-floor'), and every clean alternative with the raised track or a two-column calendar keeps heads below 52 px (e.g. 16.6 px text, heads ~49 px). Fallbacks tried first: flat and raised tracks; one-row and two-column calendars; the file's reference and title printed once in a chip instead of on the folder; the route caption moved to the band; narrower chips (0.72 and 0.55 widths) to pack fewer rows; notes placed in free space near their targets (leaders up to 260 units), singly or with one back in the band; trays widened for two-line labels; the calendar allowed down to the baseboard; trimmed side margins. Capped value: four date labels of 24 characters ('Leg 1 · Day 1 (supplied)'; baseline 19) instead of 35–38. Every other field stays at near-maximum length (parties, roles, three stops, trays, calendar title, route caption, file reference and title, both state chips, two notes).
